standard_prerequisites.name: Recursion principle of the set-quotient
standard_prerequisites.statement: For a set B and a map f : A -> B that respects R, there is fbar : A/R -> B with fbar(q(a)) := f(a).
standard_prerequisites.use: It defines the quasi-inverse of precomposition with q at source lines 1227-1229, and its computation rule is exactly the right-inverse statement at line 1230.

standard_prerequisites.name: Surjectivity of the quotient map
standard_prerequisites.statement: For every x : A/R there merely exists a : A with q(a) = x.
standard_prerequisites.use: It supplies the point a at source line 1233 that lets the left-inverse computation begin.

standard_prerequisites.name: Mere propositions and the truncation of the goal
standard_prerequisites.statement: If the goal type is a mere proposition then a merely existentially quantified hypothesis may be used purely, i.e. one may assume an actual witness.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is what turns the merely existing a at source line 1233 into a usable witness at 1234.

core_obligations: Define the quasi-inverse of precomposition with q on a pair (f, s) by the recursion principle of A/R, setting fbar(q(a)) := f(a) (source lines 1227-1229).
Observe that this defining equation is precisely the statement that f |-> fbar is a right inverse of composition with q (source line 1230).
For the left inverse, fix g : A/R -> B and x : A/R and set up the goal g(x) = overline(g o q)(x) (source line 1232).

Use the surjectivity of q to obtain a merely existing a : A with q(a) = x, note that the goal is a mere proposition, assume such an a purely, and compute g(x) = g(q(a)) = overline(g o q)(q(a)) = overline(g o q)(x) (source lines 1233-1234).

proof_roadmap.step: Build the inverse by quotient recursion and identify the defining equation with the right-inverse computation.
Left-inverse computation: use surjectivity of q, strip the truncation because the goal is a mere proposition, and compute on representatives.

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is Lemma 6.10.3 at source lines 1222-1225: for any set B, precomposition with q : A -> A/R is an equivalence between A/R -> B and the type of functions f : A -> B together with a proof that R-related points have equal images. The author's proof (source lines 1226-1235) has to do two different jobs: the recursion principle of the quotient gives the inverse and settles the right-inverse computation in one step (lines 1227-1230), but the left-inverse computation cannot be done on representatives directly, because an arbitrary x : A/R is not of the form q(a); it is done at lines 1232-1234 by invoking the surjectivity of q, noticing that the goal g(x) = overline(g o q)(x) is a mere proposition so that the truncation can be stripped, and only then computing on the representative a.
